land.text: the south-west (Jeolla) that Kyŏn Hwŏn seized from Silla in 892

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Unified Silla loses 24,800 km2 in 892, the size of this state's shape.

land.text: all of Later Baekje, conquered by Goryeo

successors.note: Cliopatria ends the row in 935 and starts Goryeo's whole-peninsula shape in 936.

capitals.name: Mujinju (Gwangju)
capitals.note: Kyŏn Hwŏn began his revolt in 892 'with an attack on Mujinju (today's Gwangju)'; the page says the capital was 'later moved to Wansanju', so Mujinju as the first seat is a reading. The Later Three Kingdoms page says the state 'is established at Jeonju' in 892.

capitals.name: Wansanju (Jeonju)
capitals.note: 'Kyŏn Hwŏn declared himself the king of Later Baekje and established his capital at Wansanju in 900.'

rulers.name: Gyeon Hwon (Kyŏn Hwŏn)
rulers.note: 'ruled from 892 - March 935'; called himself king of Later Baekje in 900. Overthrown by his son Kyŏn Sin-gŏm in 935.

rulers.name: Gyeon Sin-geom (Kyŏn Sin-gŏm)
rulers.note: Took the throne in 935; the kingdom 'finally fell in 936'.

correction.text: unchanged Cliopatria 892 shape; valid 892-909 only (Naju goes to Taebong in 910)

keyframe_review.note: 25,002 km2, the south-west. The page dates the revolt to 892 ('seized the cities of Wansanju and Mujinju') and the kingdom to 900. The Hubaekje infobox gives no area. Naju, inside this outline, was captured by Wang Kon in 910; so the unchanged shape is valid 892-909 only. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 892..909 from this entry's own 'valid 892-909 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]
New keyframe: '910, Wang Kŏn attacked and captured the city of Naju. Kyŏn later failed to retake it after a ten-day siege.'

correction.text: the 926 shape without Naju, plus Jinju; valid 928-936 (926-927 is hubaekje_910)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 926-935 shape is the 892 one. Corrected: Naju stays out, Jinju is added from c.928 ('One year later he took over the city of Jinju from Silla', the year after the 927 attack on Gyeongju) and the row runs to 936 ('finally fell in 936'). In 929 the page also has him cross the Nakdong and destroy Later Sabeol, with no place or boundary given, and in 930 and 934 he lost at Gochang and Hongseong.

region.text: Wansanju (Jeonju), Mujinju (Gwangju) and the south-west round them

ledger.note: 892: Kyŏn Hwŏn rebels against Silla. 'In 892, Kyŏn Hwŏn seized the cities of Wansanju and Mujinju' (Gyeon Hwon page); Later Baekje page: the infobox runs 892-936, the text dates the kingdom to 900. The region is Cliopatria's outline; neither page gives a boundary.
900: Kyŏn Hwŏn proclaims himself king of Later Baekje. 'Kyŏn Hwŏn declared himself the king of Later Baekje and established his capital at Wansanju in 900.'

910: Wang Kon takes Naju. 'In 910, Wang Kŏn attacked and captured the city of Naju. Kyŏn later failed to retake it after a ten-day siege.' The page does not say Hubaekje held it before; the failed retaking is the reason for reading it as Hubaekje's.

927: Kyŏn Hwŏn attacks the Silla capital. 'In 927, Kyŏn Hwŏn led his army himself and directly attacked the Silla capital of Gyeongju' (Later Baekje page: King Gyeongae killed and Gyeongsun installed; Taejo beaten near Daegu). The page gives no front line; the Daegu area is the contest zone.

c.928: Later Baekje takes Jinju from Silla. 'One year later he took over the city of Jinju from Silla', the year after the 927 attack on Gyeongju (the page gives no year; 928 is read from that sentence).

930: Later Baekje loses at Gochang. 'in 930, the Later Baekje troops faced a heavy defeat at the Battle of Gochang' near Andong; he lost again in 934 (page: 'another defeat in 934'). The year is the page's; ending the contest in 930 is a reading.

region.text: all of Later Baekje, passing to Goryeo

ledger.note: 936: Later Baekje falls to Goryeo. 'Kyŏn Hwŏn led Goryeo forces against his former kingdom; the armies met at Seonsan' and the kingdom 'finally fell in 936' (no month); in 935 Kyŏn Sin-gŏm had overthrown his father, who fled to Goryeo. Cliopatria ends the row in 935.

wars.name: Later Baekje's expedition to Daeya Fortress
wars.outcome: 'Kyŏn Hwŏn sent another major expedition to Taeya Fortress in 920'; no land is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Later Baekje attack on Gyeongju
wars.outcome: Kyŏn Hwŏn sacked Gyeongju, killed King Gyeongae and put Gyeongsun on the throne; Taejo was beaten near Daegu.
wars.note: The Later Baekje page links the battle to Palgong Mountain near Daegu.

wars.name: Battle of Gochang
wars.note: Goryeo's further victory at Hongseong came in 934.

wars.name: Goryeo conquest of Later Baekje
wars.outcome: After the 935 coup against Kyŏn Hwŏn, he and Wang Kon led a Goryeo army that ended the kingdom in 936.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary for any year; the western and southern edges are the coast, the others approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's Hubaekje has two identical shapes (892-925 and 926-935) and ends in 935; the pages end the state in 936 and date three changes inside the outline: Naju lost in 910 (to Taebong), Jinju gained c.928 (from Silla), the 927-930 contest round Daegu and Andong. The 892 start is the infobox/Cliopatria year; the text dates the kingdom to 900, when Kyŏn Hwŏn took the royal title and made Wansanju his capital. The first seat Mujinju is a reading. The 936 end overlaps Goryeo's 936 shape (Cliopatria's Goryeo starts in 936); the renderer should treat 936 as the year of conquest. No infobox area on the Later Baekje page. 2 pages opened (Later Baekje, Gyeon Hwon). Gazetteer lacks Naju and Jinju (listed). The Silla-side 'Later Sabeol' (destroyed 929) is a local lord and needs no dossier.
